narrative: Material PL1__MCF49247 exhibits smooth, moderately-skewed demand (CV=0.49) with a statistically significant declining trend over the observation period. Lead times are highly unstable (CV=0.71, range 0.38–5.02 days), making safety stock essential to maintain the 95% service level. A continuous-review (r,Q) policy is recommended: the storage constraint of 8,457.7 units caps the order quantity at 6,913, well below the unconstrained EOQ of 22,648, but still consolidates ordering from ~173 to ~26 orders per year yielding 82.8% cost reduction.
warnings: Unstable lead time: CV = 0.714 — active supplier monitoring required
Significant declining demand trend detected (slope = -2.56/day, p < 0.001) — review policy quarterly

research_insights.selection_rationale: Smooth demand with high but stable average volume suits a continuous-review fixed-order-quantity policy; the EOQ minimises combined ordering and holding costs while the reorder point absorbs lead-time and demand uncertainty at the target service level.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity is fully utilised at ~100%. The capacity-constrained OQ (6,913) is 69% below the unconstrained EOQ (22,648), increasing order frequency and annual ordering cost versus the true economic optimum. Any upward revision to safety stock would require a formal capacity extension request.
research_insights.escalation_flag: No MOQ-capacity infeasibility (MOQ 1,050 + SS 1,544 = 2,594 < 8,457.7). No escalation required, but near-full capacity utilisation should be flagged to the warehouse manager.
